B3b-01-diffusion-laboratory-experiment-setups

Two diffusion set-ups side by side. Left: a glass beaker of water with a purple potassium permanganate crystal at the bottom, shown at three stages (at the start, a small purple cloud around the crystal; after some time, a larger spreading cloud; after several hours, the whole beaker evenly pale purple). Right: a horizontal glass tube closed at both ends, with cotton wool at the left end and five strips of litmus paper along the tube, the three nearest the cotton wool coloured blue and the two furthest still red.
B3b-02-osmosis-plant-animal-cells

Two rows of cells comparing animal and plant cells in three solutions. Top row (red blood cells): in water, a swollen cell bursting (haemolysis); in isotonic solution, a normal biconcave cell; in strong salt solution, a shrunken cell with a spiky outline (crenation). Bottom row (plant cells with green cytoplasm and a pale blue vacuole): in water, a turgid cell with the cytoplasm pressed against the wall; in isotonic solution, a flaccid cell; in strong salt solution, a plasmolysed cell with the cytoplasm pulled away from the wall and a shrunken vacuole. Small blue arrows show water entering or leaving. Column headings and labels to add: "hypotonic (water)", "isotonic", "hypertonic (strong salt solution)", "red blood cell bursts (haemolysis)", "normal red blood cell", "crenated red blood cell", "turgid plant cell", "flaccid plant cell", "plasmolysed plant cell", "cell wall", "cell membrane", "vacuole".
B3b-03-potato-osmometer-experiment

Potato osmometer experiment shown as two set-ups side by side. Each is a peeled potato standing in a glass dish of water, with a cavity cut in its top containing sugar solution, and a pin marking the starting level. Left (raw potato,): the solution level in the cavity has risen well above the pin. Right (boiled potato,): the level is still at the pin. Small blue arrows on the left show water moving from the dish through the potato into the cavity.
B3b-04-onion-epidermis-cell-plasmolysis

Three magnified views of the same group of four red onion epidermis cells (brick-shaped, with walls, nucleus and a purple vacuole). Panel 1 in water: turgid cells, purple vacuole filling the cell. Panel 2 in strong sugar solution: plasmolysed cells, the cytoplasm and a smaller, darker purple vacuole pulled away from the cell wall, with clear spaces between wall and membrane. Panel 3 back in water: turgid cells again.
B3b-05-dicot-root-transverse-section

Transverse section of a young dicot root shown as a circle. From outside to inside: a piliferous layer with several long root hairs, a wide cortex of round parenchyma cells, a single-layered endodermis, a pericycle, and a central stele with a four-armed star-shaped xylem (coloured red-brown) and four groups of phloem (coloured green) between the arms. A small inset shows the low-power plan only.
B3b-06-dicot-stem-transverse-section

Transverse section of a young dicot stem shown as a circle, with an enlarged wedge showing one vascular bundle in detail. Low-power plan: epidermis with cuticle, collenchyma under it, a cortex, a ring of about eight vascular bundles, medullary rays between them, and a large central pith. Enlarged bundle: phloem (green) towards the outside, a thin band of cambium, and xylem (red-brown) with large vessels towards the centre, with a cap of fibres outside the phloem.
B3b-07-monocot-stem-transverse-section

Transverse section of a monocot (maize) stem: a circle filled with ground parenchyma and many small oval vascular bundles scattered throughout, more crowded near the edge. An enlarged view of one bundle shows a sclerenchyma sheath around phloem (towards the outside) and xylem with two large vessels in a "V" or face-like pattern, with no cambium.
B3b-08-xylem-phloem-longitudinal-section

Longitudinal sections of xylem and phloem side by side. Left (xylem, red-brown tones): a xylem vessel made of several cells end to end with the end walls gone, showing ring (annular), spiral and pitted lignin thickening in different parts, and beside it a tracheid with tapering ends and pits. Right (phloem, green tones): a sieve tube made of several cells joined by sieve plates with pores, thin cytoplasm and no nucleus, with a narrow companion cell beside each element containing a nucleus and dense cytoplasm. Below each, a small transverse section.
B3b-09-plant-eosin-dye-transport

The eosin experiment in three parts. Left: a balsam seedling standing with its roots in a beaker of red eosin solution, with thin red streaks visible running up the translucent stem and the leaf veins tinted red. Middle: an enlarged transverse section of the stem showing a ring of vascular bundles in which only the xylem part of each bundle is red, and the phloem, cortex and pith are unstained. Right: a transverse section of the root with only the central star-shaped xylem coloured red.
B3b-11-root-water-absorption-pathway

Transverse section through a sector of a root showing the path of water: soil particles with films of water around them, a long root hair cell growing between them, then a few layers of cortex cells, the endodermis with its Casparian strip drawn as a dark band in the walls, the pericycle and a xylem vessel in the centre. Blue arrows show water moving from the soil into the root hair, across the cortex from cell to cell and along cell walls, through the endodermis cells, and into the xylem.
B3b-12-dicot-leaf-transverse-section

Transverse section of part of a dicot leaf showing the upper epidermis with cuticle, palisade mesophyll, spongy mesophyll with large air spaces, a small vein with xylem and phloem, the lower epidermis and an open stoma between two guard cells. Blue arrows show water leaving the xylem, moving into mesophyll cells, evaporating into the air spaces, and water vapour (shown as small dots) diffusing out through the stoma into the air.
B3b-14-transpiration-pull-whole-plant

Diagram of a whole tall plant (a tree outline) with a continuous blue column of water drawn from the roots up through the xylem in the trunk to a leaf. At the top, an enlarged leaf section shows water vapour diffusing out of a stoma. In the middle, an enlarged piece of xylem vessel shows water molecules as small linked circles sticking to each other and to the vessel wall. At the bottom, an enlarged root hair shows water entering from the soil. Upward arrows along the trunk.
B3b-16-active-transport-root-hair

Close-up of a root hair cell membrane separating soil water (left, with a few scattered potassium ions drawn as small orange dots) from the cell sap (right, with many orange dots). A carrier protein in the membrane is shown in three stages: binding an ion on the outside, changing shape using ATP from a nearby mitochondrion, and releasing the ion on the inside. A thick arrow shows the movement from low to high concentration.
B3b-10-tree-trunk-ringing-experiment

The ringing experiment shown as a woody stem in two stages. Left, at the start: a young woody stem with a ring of bark removed exposing the pale wood, with arrows showing water (blue) going up through the wood and food (orange) coming down through the bark and stopping at the ring. Right, after some weeks: the bark just above the ring has swollen into a bulge, the leaves are still green, and a cut-away shows the inner bark (phloem) and wood (xylem).
